newsitem.title: CANADA: Gandalf falls on Q2 loss warning.
newsitem.headline: Gandalf falls on Q2 loss warning.

text.p: Shares in Gandalf Technologies Inc fell on both the Toronto and Nasdaq exchanges after the company warned investors that it will lose US$0.18 to US$0.21 per share in its fiscal second quarter.
"They've got some interesting technology but they have some real execution problems," said one New York analyst who asked not to be identified.

Gandalf shares were down 1.35 at 5.95 on the Toronto Stock Exchange at midday, up from a 52-week low of 5.30 earlier. On Nasdaq, the shares were down 1 at 4-5/16 after hitting a 52-week bottom of 3-7/8.
Gandalf issued a release saying it anticipated a net loss of about US$8 million to US$9 million for the second quarter of the 1997 fiscal year quarter.
The company said it reported break-even results for the same period last year, which ends September 28.
Gandalf also named Richard Busto as president and chief operating officer of the company.
Tom Vassiliades, chairman and chief executive of the company, will relinquish the title of president to Busto, who was one of the company's vice presidents.

Last year, Gandalf shares rose sharply on a wave of investor attention, particularly from players south of the border, because of the excitement surrounding integrated services digital network (ISDN) technology. ISDN is a big part of Gandalf's portfolio.
ISDN technology allows relatively fast computer network access to remote offices over a telephone line and is seen as an asset to telecommuters and companies which maintain far-flung operations.
"It's pretty obvious (why the stock is falling) and I am not surprised," said another U.S. analyst.

"Gandalf just isn't in a position to compete with the other players out there. They don't have the (distribution) channel infrastructure in place and they're too overburdened with a core base business that is falling, a service business that is falling and too many headcount," he added.
The analyst said Gandalf is still too much in turnaround mode to face more nimble competitors in a tough arena.
-- Sarah Edmonds, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8100, E-mail sarah.edmonds@reuters.com
